LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  March 26, 2019
1. A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by
  Mayor Don Kendrick at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present:

  Executive Board
  Don Kendrick, Mayor
  Robin Carder, Council Member
  Matthew Lyons, BUSD
  Ernie Dorado, Resident
  Carolyn Cockrell, BUSD

  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Eric Podley, BUSD
  Vanessa Hess, BHS Student Rep.
  Patti Latourelle, Resident
  Denise Fisher, Resident
  Jason Lorge, Resident
  Kim Svatos, Resident
  Matt Svatos, Resident
  Hollie Savage, LVPD
  Francisco Cambero, LVPD
  David Yim, Tri-City
  Isela Moreno, Tri-City
  Bill Aguirre, City of La Verne
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne

3. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the October, November, January, and
  February meetings were approved.

4. School Resource Officer  School Resource Officer (SRO) Frankie Cambero
  noted that things had been relatively quiet at the
  schools. However, SRO Cambero shared
  information involving an incident that took place at
  the high school earlier in the day. SRO Cambero
  commended the quick response and actions by both
  City and school employees and noted that the
  student involved is expected to make a full recovery.
  The group discussed what applicable resources were
  available to students, parents, and staff.

5. Vocational Programs  Mayor Kendrick provided information on the programs
  available through the Career & Technical Education
  Center or CTEC at Fairplex. CTEC is an educational
  center that provides training to increase industry-
  related skill and knowledge. Programs offered include
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes March 26, 2019, page 2

  Automotive, Visual Design, Water Technology,
  Fashion Design, Urban Farming, Culinary and
  Hospitality. The group discussed the programs and
  the continued need for local youth to have options
  outside of college. Mayor Kendrick noted that the
  programs also focus on teaching soft skills to better
  prepare participants for employment. Lastly, the
  methods of outreach and program promotion were
  discussed.

  Mark Rodgers with BUSD explained the school
  district’s programs as well as a history of how the
  programs have evolved. Currently known as Career
  Technical Education, the various pathways provide
  exposure to students into areas outside of traditional
  education curriculum.

  The group discussed other potential program areas
  including medical/health related as well as coding and
  computer programming.

6. Youth Intern/Apprentice  Resident Denise Fisher has been interested in
  exploring a new potential program involving
  internships and/or apprenticeships with local business
  for La Verne youth. While the potential for the
  program is very encouraging, there are also liability
  related and other concerns that would have to be
  addressed. City staff will continue to look at options
  for this type of a program and it is possible to pursue
  further.

7. Youth of the Year  Bill Aguirre provided information on the Youth of the
  Year Award, noting that the nomination period was
  now open. The Executive Committee will review
  nominees and select a winner prior to the April
  meeting.

8. Round Table  SRO Cambero noted the importance of showing kids
  affection.

  Jason Lorge emphasized his desire to help kids find
  their passion.

  Isela Moreno with Tri-City Mental Health shared
  information on the Public Hearing of Mental Health
  Commission being held on April 9th. Isela also
  provided information on a new Community Navigator
  for La Verne and efforts on homelessness.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes March 26, 2019, page 3

  Mark Rodgers updated the group on progress with the
  expansion of school district counseling programs.

  Matthew Lyons shared his compliments of Mark and
  the BUSD for their efforts on mental health issues and
  the district’s commitment to the community.

  Eric Podley provided information on recent training
  attended by administrators and school staff.

9.  Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting is scheduled for April 22,
  2019 at 6:30 p.m.

10. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 8:25 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

JR Ranells
Personnel Officer
